speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the onset and progression of your double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness? Specifically, when did these symptoms start, and have they been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does your double vision improve after you rest, and do you experience any difficulty swallowing or speaking that fluctuates throughout the day? I also need to know if you have any known autoimmune conditions or if there is a family history of neuromuscular diseases.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do you notice any drooping of your eyelids, especially later in the day or after prolonged visual tasks? I would like to order an Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody test to check for an autoimmune cause.
REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies, combined with your fluctuating weakness and double vision, confirms the diagnosis.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
